text: Swimming requires specific abilities; first is wearing goggles to shield the eyes and exclude water from them. These devices typically consist of light, flexible materials fitted tightly over the head. Their function includes preventing irritation or injury caused by water, reducing drag, and enhancing aquatic performance. Next, swimmers must master laps, which means swimming a set distance or completing a timed segment continuously. This action occurs in freestyle, breaststroke, backstroke, or butterfly styles, whether performed within the pool or along the lane on the deck. Through dedicated practice, any individual can acquire swimming proficiency and execute laps correctly.
